profile.reading:
Intergate Seattle East Building 1 is part of Sabey Data Centers' Tukwila, Washington campus, which Sabey markets today as a single site called SDC Seattle, a few miles south of downtown Seattle and about three miles from Sea-Tac International Airport. Building 1 sits in the cluster of buildings along South 120th Place that Sabey and public mapping data still refer to as the Intergate.East side of the site, alongside Building 2 at 3311 South 120th Place and Building 3 at 3333 South 120th Place. No street address specific to Building 1 was found in this pass, only its coordinates placing it a short distance from those two neighboring buildings on the same block.

Sabey Data Centers is the data center subsidiary of Sabey Corporation, a Puget Sound commercial real estate and construction company founded in 1972 by Dave Sabey that built its early business as a major industrial and office landlord in the Seattle area through the aerospace driven growth of the 1970s and 1980s. Sabey's own company history describes its move into data centers as tracing back to a tenant vacating one of its buildings during the dot com collapse of the early 2000s, leaving Sabey with an empty large scale technical shell, now counted as SDC Seattle Building 5, that the company recognized as an opportunity in a market starting to demand purpose built computing space. Sabey formalized that pivot in 2010 by partnering with institutional investor National Real Estate Advisors to create Sabey Data Centers as a dedicated operating company, which today describes its national portfolio as more than four million square feet of mission critical space across six campuses in Washington, New York, Texas, and Virginia, with more in development.

On power and scale, Sabey's own site describes SDC Seattle as a whole running on hydroelectric power delivered by Seattle City Light, with more than 90 MVA of aggregate utility power delivered to the campus through redundant feeds, backup generators rated at 2.5 MW apiece with 72 hour runtime at peak load, about 9,500 tons of installed HVAC capacity, and over a million square feet of total space. These figures describe the entire Tukwila site, covering both the Intergate.East cluster where Building 1 sits and the separate Intergate.West cluster of buildings on Tukwila International Boulevard, not any single building within it, and Sabey does not publish a building level IT load, utility power, or generator count specific to Building 1. Sabey's certifications for the SDC Seattle campus as a whole include HIPAA and HITECH alignment, PCI DSS, SSAE 18 SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2, LEED Gold, and ISO 27001, again applied at the campus level rather than to individual buildings.

No King County Assessor parcel record, City of Tukwila building permit, or construction and occupancy date specific to Building 1 was identified in this pass, and no trade press coverage naming this building individually, as opposed to the SDC Seattle campus as a whole, was found either.
profile.capacity_note: not published at the building level. Campus wide total is 54 MW (operator figure) across the Tukwila campus, not applied to this individual building.
profile.research_note: WebSearch was exhausted this session (200 of 200) before this facility group, so research relied on direct WebFetch of Sabey Data Centers' own site (locations page, about page, homepage) plus the facility's own OSM address tags already stored in this database's osm_tags column, which supplied the confirmed South 120th Place addresses for neighboring Buildings 2 and 3 but had no address tag for Building 1 itself. Sabey's current marketing treats the whole Tukwila property as one campus, SDC Seattle, and does not break out East vs West sub campus figures or per building specs, so the campus_power_note here reuses the same figures already on file for sibling Building 2 (osm:way/205724881) for consistency across the campus. The Boeing-purchase and 1999-reacquisition narrative present in Building 2's existing profile could not be independently reverified via Sabey's own site this pass (that page describes only a generic dot-com era vacancy, not Boeing by name), so it is not repeated here to avoid restating an unconfirmed specific. No King County Assessor or City of Tukwila permit data was accessible.

profile.campus_power_note: SDC Seattle / Intergate East campus wide figures, not assigned to any single building including this one. Per Data Center Dynamics, 2025: 54 MW total capacity across roughly 1.2 million square feet, six buildings, plus 6 MW of additional Tier III critical power the operator said was scheduled online by December 1, 2025. Per Sabey Data Centers' own site: more than 90 MVA of aggregate utility power delivered through redundant feeds, backup generators rated 2.5 MW apiece with 72 hour runtime at peak load, and about 9,500 tons of installed HVAC capacity across the campus.

reading.body:
Intergate Seattle East Building 1 is part of Sabey Data Centers' Tukwila campus, which the operator markets as SDC Seattle and spans six buildings totaling more than a million square feet. The campus sits a few miles south of downtown Seattle and three miles from Sea-Tac International Airport, drawing power from Seattle City Light via redundant feeds and hydroelectric generation. Building 1 sits within the Intergate.East cluster on South 120th Place, but Sabey does not publish IT load, power draw, or generator capacity at the building level.

The Tukwila campus as a whole has 54 MW of published power capacity across its footprint, with 6 MW additional capacity scheduled online by December 1, 2025. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 54 MW of IT load would support roughly 1,350 racks, though this figure applies to the entire six-building campus, not to Building 1 alone. The campus draws from 90 MVA of aggregate utility power through redundant feeds, runs backup generators at 2.5 MW per unit with 72 hour runtime, and maintains 9,500 tons of HVAC capacity for cooling. The facility holds HIPAA, HITECH, PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, LEED Gold, and ISO 27001 certifications at the campus level.

This campus ranks third in Washington state by published megawatt capacity, behind two other facilities, and represents one of only two data centers in the state with operator-published power figures. No building-level specification was found for Building 1 individually, and without published capacity assignment to this facility, its individual scale for AI deployment cannot be determined from available sources.
